title: Walaeus & Mestrezat: we are justified by receiving Christ, not by believing remission already past
source_text: CXXI. Praeterea his adjungimus Antonium Walaeum, qui negat Actum primum fidei quo justificamur, esse actum illum quo creditur remissio peccatorum, sed quo recipitur Christus cum merito ejus, in remissionem peccatorum, non praeteritam, sed sequentem; atque istud non tam per assensum particularem, quam per fiduciam illam voluntatis a generali assensu sequitur. Nec alia potest esse mens Joannis Mestrezatii, cui fides justificans definitur perfugium peccatoris poenitentis ad Dei misericordiam in Christo.
pass_a_gloss: Besides these we add Antony Walaeus, who denies that the first act of faith by which we are justified is that act by which remission of sins is believed, but that by which Christ with his merit is received unto remission of sins — not past, but following; and that this follows not so much through particular assent as through that trust of the will which follows general assent. Nor can John Mestrezat's mind be otherwise, for whom justifying faith is defined as the refuge of the penitent sinner to God's mercy in Christ.
pass_b_english: Walaeus: the first justifying faith-act is receiving Christ with his merit unto coming remission — not believing remission already past — via will's trust after general assent.
Mestrezat's definition matches: justifying faith is the penitent sinner's refuge to God's mercy in Christ.
